record.context_brief: Lower bounds for sparse perfect state transfer graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with m edges and diameter D, and let U(t) = exp(itA) be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G, where A is the adjacency matrix of G. Suppose G admits perfect state transfer between two vertices. Prove a supercubic lower bound on the number of edges in terms of the diameter; specifically, show that m belongs to Omega(D^k) for some exponent k > 3.

evidence.quote: If we think of edges in a graph as corresponding to interactions between qubits, then, for the purposes of implementation, it would be more economical to minimize the number of edges, while preserving the behaviour. In this vein, one might ask for the graph on n vertices with the least number of edges such that there is perfect state transfer between some two vertices.
2.1 Open Problem. If perfect state transfer occurs in a graph with m edges of diameter D, show that m ∈ Ω(D^k), for k > 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple connected graph with adjacency matrix $A$, having $m$ edges and diameter $D$. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is defined by the unitary transition matrix $U(t) = \exp(itA)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$. We say that $G$ admits perfect state transfer between distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ if there exists a real number $\tau > 0$ and a unimodular complex number $\gamma$ such that $U(\tau) e_u = \gamma\, e_v$, where $e_u, e_v$ denote the standard basis vectors indexed by $u$ and $v$.

Prove a supercubic lower bound for the number of edges of such a graph in terms of its diameter: namely, establish that there exists an exponent $k > 3$ such that whenever $G$ admits perfect state transfer between some pair of vertices and has diameter $D$, then 
$$m \in \Omega(D^{k}).$$
artifact.category_tag: perfect state transfer in quantum walks
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among selected open problems on continuous-time quantum walks. Known constructions of graphs admitting perfect state transfer yield families whose number of edges grows roughly cubically in the diameter, and improving the lower bound beyond cubic remains unresolved as of recent surveys (2024–2025).

status_evidence.title: Selected open problems in continuous-time quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: A key open problem concerns the growth rate of edges with respect to diameter; the number of edges in a certain family of graphs grows cubic in the diameter, and any improvement on the cubic bound should probably depend on all conditions in the characterization of PST.
status_evidence.claim: The supercubic lower bound m ∈ Ω(D^k) with k > 3 for graphs with perfect state transfer is recorded as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Peak state transfer in continuous quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of graph families admitting perfect state transfer with size polynomial in diameter; the cubic bound persists.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still references the cubic edge–diameter relationship as the state of the art.
